records.issue_text: The 'already an attendee' check and createMany are not in a transaction, so concurrent requests or double-submit can add duplicate attendees, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) to prevent it
Errors from sendAddGuestsEmails are swallowed with a bare console.log that doesn't even log the err object, so guests may be added with no email notification and no surfaced failure
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows any failure and does not log/propagate the `err`. The diff shows guests are still persisted and calendar attendees updated even if email delivery fails, with no surfaced error beyond a generic log line.

records.issue_text: Attendee-existence check is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so Foo@x.com passes as 'new' when foo@x.com already exists, creating a duplicate attendee differing only by case
